gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu keeps its s curves wide and its text quiet. Tektur sits above it, bending every letter like pipe cleaner with outsized lowercase, so the two feel like a loud voice next to a patient one.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Tektur bends its s curves like wire, never thinning at the spine, and that gives the heading a bold mechanical personality. Noto Sans Lydian is friendlier, with capitals barely taller than lowercase, and its softness is what makes the pair work.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Tektur's tails and terminals are as thick as its main stems, which gives the heading a chunky, built-from-tubing look. And Noto Sans Mahajani follows with tall lowercase and a funnel-wide e, so the page moves from rugged to open.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Expressive is the right word for Tektur, whose single stroke width runs through the whole alphabet like bent wire. Noto Sans Malayalam settles beneath it with a dense middle zone and an s that opens generously, so the page eases from showy to approachable.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Wire-bent and oversized, Tektur glides along on a stroke weight that never changes. Noto Sans Mandaic matches that ease best, its curvy lowercase rising close to the capitals and feeling pleasantly unclamped beside the heading.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Tektur draws pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin. Noto Sans Marchen follows with small letters standing almost capital-sized and curves ending in clear daylight, so the page turns from sketchy and expressive to crisp and open.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-mayan-numeral: Distinctive describes Tektur, whose plain constant-width lines and generous curve openings make the heading feel like cut and bent wire. Give Noto Sans Mayan Numerals a bit more size, since its gaping c wants room.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-medefaidrin: Noto Sans Medefaidrin brings lowercase that rises high and curves that turn in without any ink pooling, a sharp contrast to the heading. Tektur's rounded strokes look like cut lengths of cord, and they would feel cramped if made small.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Cut-wire letters with outsized lowercase, that is Tektur, and its diagonals are as thick as its horizontals. But Noto Sans Meetei Mayek has rounds that gap like a cracked bangle, and a small heading would lose that tension.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Tektur shares one thickness between its stems and crossbars, and its curves open generously at every terminal, giving the heading an engineered feel. Noto Sans Mende Kikakui adds daylight through every curve and tall lowercase, so the two read as one family of shapes.
